module: Disclose biometric exposure and published content

lesson.title: Published text on matters of public interest
lesson.summary: Identify publication intended to inform the public on matters of public interest.

prerequisites.reason: The learner must identify the actor using the system under its authority.
The learner must recognise generated or manipulated output and its modality.

blocks: For AI-generated or manipulated **text**, the paragraph 4 disclosure rule concerns text published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest. These conditions must be examined together.

A **matter of public interest** concerns issues relevant to public life and collective interests. The guidance discusses fields such as politics, health, security, environmental matters and financial or economic issues. A topic label alone does not establish the whole publication test.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(4), subparagraph 2, sentence 1; Guidelines paragraphs 130-132
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation

blocks: A private customer-service answer or internal email is not automatically a publication to inform the public. A public safety article assembled from those answers can have a different purpose and audience.

Harbour uses AI to draft an internal operational email and a website article informing residents about a pollution incident. The public-facing environmental article needs the specified published-text analysis.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(4), subparagraph 2, sentence 1; Guidelines paragraphs 130-132
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation

blocks: A cookbook or ordinary promotional text is not automatically within this specific duty merely because it is public. Health claims, safety advice or reporting on collective interests can change the analysis.
Use the actual content, audience, purpose and publication context. Record uncertainty where facts are missing, rather than declaring all public AI text either covered or exempt.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(4), subparagraph 2, sentence 1; Guidelines paragraphs 130-132
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation

blocks: This lesson identifies the publication trigger; the following lesson examines the human-review/editorial exception. The provider's paragraph 2 machine-readable marking duty is separate and may still apply to generated text outside this particular paragraph 4 trigger.

Harbour's publication worksheet asks: is it generated or manipulated text, is it published, is its purpose to inform the public, and does the matter involve public interest? A private-to-public reuse requires a new assessment.

questions.prompt: Harbour publishes an AI-drafted article informing residents about a pollution incident. Which characteristic is relevant to the public-interest assessment?

options.reason: Environmental and collective interests are relevant, alongside purpose and publication.
